text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone is not evidence. Four women on a panel is unremarkable in HR-involved hiring and tells you nothing about how they scored candidates; raising it as your opening move signals grievance rather than substance, and it is the easiest claim for them to dismiss.

Also, your case on merit is weaker than it feels. Years of experience and project leadership matter, but "head of group" at a consultancy is substantially a business-development role, and client relationships are a legitimate — often decisive — criterion. Eight years with a chartership is not thin.

The real problem is the ignored request. Chase it in writing, ask for your scores against the published criteria, and judge the decision on what comes back.
